title: Determinism: a foundational DS guarantee
preamble:
# Determinism: a foundational DS guarantee

A foundational language-level guarantee. DS is **deterministic
under a fixed three-tuple**: same compiled rule set, same
event trace, same platform → same observable output, every
time, byte-for-byte.

Platform is the third bound, not a footnote. Within one
platform the guarantee is absolute; **across platforms it is also
absolute** — every operation the language admits is exact or
correctly rounded (64-bit integer arithmetic, the IEEE `+ − × ÷ √`,
and the transcendentals, [LEXP.3.9.2]), so rule firing order and
every computed value are byte-identical on every conforming target.

This is not a performance property or an implementation hint.
It is a spec-level commitment the language makes to every rule
author and every tool that interacts with DS. Testing
([LTES]) and debugging ([LDEB]) both depend on
it. A runtime that cannot honour it on its own platform is not
a conforming DS runtime.

## What this is not

- Not a claim about wall-clock reproducibility. The clock is
  input, not output (see [LTES]); two runs that use the same clock schedule produce
  the same output, but wall-clock latency between two
  observable events isn't bounded by this guarantee.
- Not a claim about performance parity. Runtime-internal
  choices (scheduling, caching, Rete-memory layout) may differ
  across implementations as long as observable output matches.
